full_judgment: 18. In some other laws, like the Pourashava Ordinance, 1977 the Government has been given plenary powers to extend, curtail or otherwise alter the limit of any municipality (section 4(b) of the Pourashava Ordinance, 1977) but this power was made subject to the limitation by providing a pre-condition in the words: "The Government may, in the prescribed manner". Thus, the plenary powers in this section of the Pourashava Ordinance, 1977 is plenary but not absolute, for, it must be exercised in the "prescribed manner". So, this is the check and balance of power. Where there is power that power must be exercised with some restrictions and in a prescribed balanced manner to the knowledge of all.
